title: Acyclicity of injective finite-torsion coefficients after scalar extension
statement: Let k and K be algebraically closed fields with K a k-algebra, f:X -> Spec k quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and n a natural number with (n:k) nonzero. For every injective etale ULift(Z/n)-module sheaf J on X and every positive degree q, the underlying abelian cohomology of the module inverse image of J on X_K is zero (a subsingleton group). This is acyclicity only for injective coefficients; it does not assert comparison for the constant sheaf or arbitrary coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 59.90.1, applied to an injective module sheaf; Tags 03FD and 03QU supply source and base acyclicity

proof.text: Identify J as a module over the constant ring sheaf, preserving injectivity and its underlying abelian sheaf. The injective-module direct-image acyclicity theorem directly makes every positive rightDerived q along f zero. Sectionwise n kills J and its underlying sheaf. This avoids any source-global-cohomology comparison or conservativity argument.

Apply the specialized higher-direct-image field exchange. Exact inverse image of the zero source higher image is zero, so the corresponding higher image on Spec K is zero. The field exchange is constructed from smooth subalgebras of K/k and affine inverse-limit continuity.

Global sections on the separably closed Spec K are exact: compare with sections at its terminal etale point, use preservation of epimorphisms and kernels, and infer finite-colimit preservation. Its derived functor agrees with its exact derived functor. Derived Leray and exact-functor homology comparison give zero cohomology of the pullback sheaf. Compare this with Sheaf.H and transport along the module-forgetting inverse-image isomorphism. The target signature, n=1, n=0 exclusion and empty X are unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 59.90.1, perfect-base smooth-subalgebra route; direct injective higher-image acyclicity and exact global sections on Spec K (X2, 2026-10-14)
